feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. It is the iteration 5 design (best raced, score 851.5: oval 20/20, s-bend 20/20, slalom 11/20) with two changes. Mass drops from 0.45 to 0.40 kg, the contract lower bound. Iteration 3 to 5 showed that cutting mass from 0.6 to 0.45 lowered slalom max_error and line-loss events while the oval and s-bend improved, so continuing that trend is a reasonable test. All five sensors move forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.06 m. This is the lead lever the previous Evaluator review named after the mass change, and it has not been tested before. The sensor y change is untested, and the two changes together will not be separable on slalom, so read the result as a pair. Sensor x positions, 16 mm size, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], kp 4.0, kd 1.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction line loss are unchanged from iteration 5. Kp stays at 4.0 because iteration 4 (kp 6.0 with a 7-sensor array) and iteration 2 (kp 4.5) both cost oval and s-bend completion. The approval is for an early-to-mid exploration iteration with 5 iterations left, so racing this candidate gives the telemetry needed to isolate the next lever. Plan the revision from the race telemetry as follows. If oval or s-bend completion drops below 100% and 100% respectively, or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, the lighter robot is under-damped: return mass to 0.45 and keep the sensor lead. If slalom still leaves the track more than about 5 times in 20 with max_error near or above 0.042, raise kd to about 1.2 before touching kp. If slalom finishes but times out, the timeouts point to speed, so test base_speed in steps of 0.1.
requested_changes: If oval or s-bend completion falls below iteration 5 (100% and 100%), or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, return geometry.mass to 0.45 and keep the sensor lead at y = 0.06. Basis: iteration 5 showed that mass 0.45 held both tracks at 100% with steering_oscillation of 0.23 to 0.31, and a lighter robot has less yaw damping.

If slalom still has 5 or more off-track exits out of 20 with max_error near or above 0.042, raise controller.kd from 1.0 to about 1.2 and keep kp at 4.0. Basis: iteration 5 slalom had 7 off-track exits and max_error 0.042, and kp increases in iterations 2 and 4 cost oval and s-bend completion, so kd is the untested damping lever.

If slalom completes but still shows timeouts, raise controller.base_speed in steps of 0.1 (1.5 to 1.6) while holding the gains. Basis: iteration 5 had 2 slalom timeouts and a mean finish time of 2.92 s against the 3.0 s limit, and iteration 0 at base_speed 1.6 showed the oval still finishing in about 1.9 s.
